title: Singapore workers embrace AI faster than global peers, but fewer feel secure in their jobs: PwC survey
key_facts: In PwC's Global Workforce Hopes and Fears Survey 2026, 69 percent of Singapore respondents were moderately to extremely confident about job security over the next 12 months, down from 72 percent in 2025 and 84 percent in 2024; the global figure was 84 percent in 2026, 85 percent in 2025 and 84 percent in 2024.
Confidence was 75 percent among daily gen AI users in Singapore and 61 percent among those who had not used AI at work in the past year.
The Singapore edition, released on Monday 12 Oct 2026, draws on 1,000 local respondents out of 49,364 workers in 48 territories surveyed in May and June 2026.
74 percent of Singapore respondents used AI at work in the previous 12 months (69 percent in 2025), against a global average of 64 percent; daily gen AI use was 28 percent versus 22 percent globally.

72 percent said AI improved the quality of their work, but only 32 percent said it helps with the most complex parts of their job; about 50 percent said AI had increased the complexity of their work and 46 percent said it added to their workload.
Economic volatility was the top threat to job security over the next three years (60 percent), with AI taking on more tasks second at 53 percent, against 44 percent globally.
Pay and benefits were the top job priority for 65 percent of Singapore respondents; 45 percent found the amount and speed of change difficult to manage, against 42 percent globally.

PwC Singapore signed a memorandum of understanding with the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) to help companies create better jobs as they adopt AI, and joins NTUC's AI-Ready SG initiative as a lead multiplier.
quote_evidence: Workers in Singapore are using artificial intelligence more than their global peers, but their confidence in job security has fallen sharply over the past two years, while confidence globally has held steady.
Some 74 per cent of local respondents used AI at work in the previous 12 months, up from 69 per cent in 2025 and above the global average of 64 per cent.

“Our research shows that Singapore workers are already seeing tangible benefits from AI, yet many remain uncertain about what it means for their future,” said PwC Singapore executive chairman and chief executive Marcus Lam.
why_it_matters_hint: Heavy AI use at work in Singapore has not made workers there feel safer in their jobs; their confidence is 15 points below 2024 while the global figure is unchanged.
notes: Survey figures are PwC's own, relayed by The Business Times; the Singapore sample is 1,000 people. Survey is self-reported.
